environment: Python 3.14.7, Node 24.19.0, gh and glab shims from the testkit stub-server on PATH, scratch git repos, no network

cases.title: Public surface: derive(rules), suggest(rules, rows, derived), _regex_literal(rule) exist
cases.given: branches.py loaded by path with python3 -I

cases.title: derive returns the three table formats for the spec examples
cases.then: feature/sdlc/{name}, sdlc/{name}-x, sdlc/team/{name}, plus release/, .lock, a..b
cases.expected: feature/sdlc/{name}, sdlc/{name}-x, sdlc/team/{name}, plus release/, .lock, a..b

evidence.title: examples

cases.title: CLI derives for each operator in pr mode and exits 0 with second-verdict samples
cases.given: gh stub with one rule, no format
cases.then: ok true, derived true, derived format, every sample pass, exit 0, stderr empty
cases.expected: ok true, derived true, derived format, every sample pass, exit 0, stderr empty
cases.actual: starts_with feature/, ends_with -x, contains team, starts_with team/sub/ all derived; exit 0

cases.title: A rule the default format already passes does not derive
cases.then: ok true, derived false, default format, exit 0
cases.expected: ok true, derived false, default format, exit 0

cases.title: Property: derive equals a table reference model over random rule lists
cases.given: 3000 generated rule lists: 0 to 3 rules, kinds incl. regex, bogus, upper-case, null; patterns incl. unicode, brace, newline, 10000 chars; non-string patterns; negate
cases.then: string from the table for exactly one non-negated table kind with a non-empty string pattern, else None; never raises
cases.expected: string from the table for exactly one non-negated table kind with a non-empty string pattern, else None; never raises

cases.title: derive and suggest are deterministic and do not mutate their input
cases.then: equal results, inputs equal to the copy
cases.expected: equal results, inputs equal to the copy

cases.title: CLI refuses derivation for a given flag format, a config format, a negated rule, a regex rule, two rules, an unknown kind; zero rules gives the default
cases.then: derived false, the original format, exit 1 (or 0 when the default passes), no stderr
cases.expected: derived false, the original format, exit 1 (or 0 when the default passes), no stderr

cases.title: mr and direct mode never derive; a bad --branch in mr mode gives one rename line
cases.then: derived false, format sdlc/{name}; mr: exit 1, one-line rename suggestion, no --branch-format
cases.expected: derived false, format sdlc/{name}; mr: exit 1, one-line rename suggestion, no --branch-format

cases.title: pr and stack mode derive when a loop-kind sample fails
suggest with a loop row and a working row gives two lines, format first; working alone gives the rename alone; no rule gives the check-ref-format line; derived row gives the derived line
cases.actual: two lines [--branch-format "feature/{name}" (rule "rx": regex "..."), rename the branch "bad name" ...]; others as expected

evidence.title: suggest outputs
evidence.inline:
two: --branch-format "feature/{name}" (rule "rx": regex "^(feature|bugfix)/[A-Z]+-\d+$")\nrename the branch "bad name" (rule "rx"), for example: git branch -m bad name <new-name>
derived: --branch-format "release/sdlc/{name}"
generic: --branch-format "<prefix>{name}<suffix>" (every branch name must pass: git check-ref-format)

cases.title: Property: a failing row always gives a non-empty suggestion, format line first, one line per cause, no raise
cases.given: 2000 generated rule and row lists, incl. newline and quote names
cases.then: non-empty exactly when a row failed; line count equals the cause count; format line first
cases.expected: non-empty exactly when a row failed; line count equals the cause count; format line first

cases.title: CLI: negated rule, two rules, given format, and no rule with an invalid ref format
cases.then: exit 1 and a --branch-format suggestion; the invalid ref format exits 2 with a JSON error
cases.expected: exit 1 and a --branch-format suggestion; the invalid ref format exits 2 with a JSON error

cases.title: mr mode working failure for branch names with spaces, quotes, dashes, $(), backslash: exit 1, one rename line, no stderr
cases.then: rename line names the branch; exit 1
cases.expected: rename line names the branch; exit 1
cases.actual: as expected. The line puts the name in double quotes, then unquoted after git branch -m (see seed)

evidence.title: rename lines
evidence.inline:
"bad name" => rename the branch "bad name" (rule "push rule"), for example: git branch -m bad name <new-name>
"--force" => ... git branch -m --force <new-name>
"$(id)" => ... git branch -m $(id) <new-name>

cases.title: CLI regex rules in pr and stack mode give a literal that the rule accepts at S-001, with the pattern quoted
cases.given: 14 patterns incl. alternation, classes, groups, repeats with minimum 0, dot, anchors, non-capturing groups
cases.when: preflight --mode pr / stack, then re.search(pattern, literal + '/S-001') in a separate Python
cases.then: literal accepted; pattern quoted; text fallback otherwise
cases.expected: literal accepted; pattern quoted; text fallback otherwise
cases.actual: every literal accepted: feature, user-a, a, feat, y, ac; seven patterns used the text fallback; one pattern passed by default

cases.title: Unsatisfiable, unparseable and unusual regex rules never crash and give the quoted-pattern text
cases.given: ^[a-z]+$, lookahead, backreference, (?i) flag, \p{L}, invalid patterns, empty pattern
cases.then: exit 0 or 1, empty stderr; text fallback quotes the pattern
cases.expected: exit 0 or 1, empty stderr; text fallback quotes the pattern
cases.actual: (?i)^FEATURE/ gives literal FEATURE; the others give the text fallback or an unevaluated note; no traceback

cases.title: _regex_literal on repeat counts and nesting that finish quickly returns without raising
cases.given: 8 hostile patterns incl. a{4294967295}, (a{9999}){9999}, (a*)*b, 500 nested groups, 200000 characters
cases.actual: no exception for any of the eight
cases.specSource: R-122 acceptance (no timing limit in the spec)

cases.title: Property: every literal that _regex_literal returns is accepted by the rule at the S-001 tail and passes validate_format

seeds.title: _regex_literal builds a huge string for large repeat counts
seeds.detail: For a regex rule that holds a large repeat count, _shortest multiplies the inner string by the count. a{999999999} took 17.5 s and 5.7 GB resident memory. ((a{1000}){1000}){1000} took 18.6 s and 5.9 GB. (?:x{65535}){65535} did not finish in 40 s. Through the CLI, ^a{999999999}/ and ^((a{1000}){1000}){1000}/ each took about 20 s before preflight printed the text fallback. A cap on the built length would bound this. The spec states no limit.

seeds.title: A derived format that validate_format refuses is reported as ok
seeds.detail: derive builds the format from the pattern and the second verdict does not call validate_format. A starts_with, ends_with or contains rule with the pattern { or } or {x} gives ok true, derived true and a format such as {sdlc/{name}. validate_format refuses that format (brace outside its placeholder), so the next run that reads it as --format or branchFormat exits 2.

seeds.title: Rename line puts the branch name unquoted after git branch -m
seeds.detail: The line reads: rename the branch "<name>" (rule "<rule>"), for example: git branch -m <name> <new-name>. A name with a space, a leading dash or $(...) gives a command that breaks or runs differently when pasted. The name is not escaped inside the double quotes either.

seeds.title: A pattern with a newline splits the suggestion into two lines
seeds.detail: starts_with, ends_with or contains with the pattern x<newline>y fails the derived format and the suggestion holds the raw pattern, so the output has two lines. The quoted regex pattern and labels are also unescaped (a double quote inside a pattern ends the quote early). The suggestion is a JSON string, so only a consumer that splits lines is affected.

seeds.title: A non-string pattern in a rule crashes preflight with a traceback
seeds.detail: A starts_with rule whose pattern is a list gives TypeError in _raw_result (S-015 code, not in the S-016 diff). Exit 1 with a traceback and no JSON. The derive function refuses such a rule, so the crash is before the S-016 code runs. The forge API gives string patterns.

seeds.title: An empty-prefix regex candidate is skipped
seeds.detail: For ^a*/S-1$ the shortest match is /S-1, so the only cut gives an empty candidate and the text fallback appears, although a/S-1 would pass the rule. A rule with minimum 0 before the first slash always falls back to text. This matches the plan, which says the fallback is acceptable.

seeds.title: A bare --branch value that starts with a dash is refused by argparse
seeds.detail: --branch -x exits 2 with 'expected one argument'. --branch=-x works. The rename path was verified with the = form.
